narrative: In this stylized demo—which is not an engineering estimate—a magnitude 5.5 earthquake coupled with a 17.32-foot compound storm tide initiates a severe cascade across the waterfront network. Perimeter seawall breaches (49% probability) directly compromise electric substations (53%), fuel handling, and bridge approaches. Power loss then propagates through high dependency weights to disable high-pressure water pumps and communications, culminating in widespread failure of the multi-dependent ferry terminal (71%) and evacuation roads (61%). These compounding downstream outages drive the 1-in-100 tail risk of $1.28 billion VaR. The proposed fixes break this chain at the source through deep soil mixing, parapet extensions, and pneumatic floodgates at the seawall, while elevated, base-isolated substations and local microgrids decouple critical lifelines from cascading outages.
